result.summary: The image shows a residential intersection with a high-visibility continental crosswalk and ADA-compliant curb ramps with tactile paving. While basic infrastructure is present, the lack of visible pedestrian signals and potential sightline obstructions from mature street trees are notable safety concerns.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: A large tree at the corner may obstruct the view between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-right, near the traffic light pole.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicular signals which may not provide adequate clearance time.
hazards.location_in_image: Traffic light pole at the corner.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on crossing time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight, past the obstruction of the tree.

result.summary: The image depicts a residential street with a marked zebra crosswalk and sidewalks on both sides. While basic infrastructure like a bike lane and crossing markings are present, the crossing is uncontrolled and lacks physical traffic calming or active warning signals.

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Crossing
hazards.description: The marked crosswalk lacks any stop control, traffic signals, or flashing beacons to assist pedestrians in crossing a two-lane road.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Dense, low-hanging tree foliage on the right side of the image may obscure pedestrians waiting to cross from the view of approaching motorists.

hazards.name: Roadway Surface Degradation
hazards.description: Significant longitudinal and transverse cracking in the asphalt within the crosswalk area could present a minor tripping hazard.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position before they enter the roadway.

interventions.title: Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacon (RRFB)
interventions.description: Add pedestrian-activated flashing beacons to increase driver yielding rates at this uncontrolled mid-block crossing.

interventions.title: Vegetation Management
interventions.description: Trim low-hanging tree branches near the crossing to ensure clear sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure like sidewalks and curb ramps, but lacks marked crosswalks across the primary thoroughfare. The wide, unmarked roadway and absence of visible pedestrian signals increase exposure and risk for people crossing the main street.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: The primary crossing across the main road lacks painted markings, making pedestrian movements less predictable to drivers.

hazards.name: Wide Unmarked Roadway
hazards.description: The lack of lane markings on a wide road surface can lead to higher vehicle speeds and irregular lane positioning.

hazards.name: Sight Line Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the side street may partially block the view of pedestrians waiting to cross.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style crosswalk markings across all legs of the intersection to clearly define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the corners to reduce crossing distance and improve sight lines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Add dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on crossing time.

result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure including a sidewalk and a curb ramp, but safety is compromised by significantly faded crosswalk markings. While a traffic signal is present, there are no visible dedicated pedestrian signals or high-visibility crossing treatments to protect people crossing the wide side street.
